07. 1.
Notice had been issued to the informant on 12.01.2024 by both ways (through the local Police Station as well as by the Registered post).

As necessary postal stamp had not been filed by the petitioner, notice could not be issued to the informant through registered post, for which on 15.02.2024 time had been granted till 19.02.2024 to make good the shortage in postal stamp.
Thereafter, from the office note it appears that notice was issued to the informant on 21.03.2024.
Postal tracking report attached to the file reveals that notice has been Page1 of 6 delivered on the addressee on 30.03.2024.

Unfortunately, the Dealing Assistant who has prepared the note sheet has failed to give necessary noting after 19.04.2024, for which the physical file had to be referred to and the office notes had to be examined.

2. Mr. B. Tripathy, learned Additional Standing Counsel submits that notice which has been sent to the informant (brother of the victim) through the local Police Station, has been served on him on 20.03.2024.
Since notice has been served on the informant both through Registered post as well as through the local Police Station, notice is deemed to be sufficient on the informant.

3. This application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. has been filed in connection with Bolagarh P.S. Case No. 208 of 2023 corresponding to G.R. Case No. 871 of 2023 where the accused is facing trial for commission of offences punishable under Sections 363,366,376(2)(n),34 of the IPC, read with Section 6 of the POCSO Act in the Court of the learned Additional Sessions judge, (POCSO),
Bhubaneswar in TR Case No. 440 of 2023.

sentences.text: The prayer for bail of the petitioner and co-accused Sanjubala Swain @ Sanju has been rejected on 19.10.2023 by the learned Additional Sessions judge-cum-Special Judge, (POCSO), Bhubaneswar on the ground that if they are enlarged on bail, there is likelihood of their absconding and intimidating of prosecution witnesses.
5. This bail application has been listed before me as BLAPL No. 12440 of 2023 filed by the co-accused (his mother) Sanjubala Swain had been disposed of by me on 07.11.2023.

6. Perused the report dated 08.05.2024 of the learned Additional Sessions Judge-cum-Special Judge (POCSO), Bhubaneswar, who has stated that out of 20 charge sheet witnesses, 3 witnesses including the victim have been examined in the case and summons have been issued to rest of the witnesses for their examination and the case is posted to 07.05.2024.
7.
The prosecution allegation in brief is that the petitioner was working as a painter and had come to the village of the informant for doing painting work in the temple.
Thereafter, he took the Instagram ID of the victim as well as her Phone Page3 of 6 number and was chatting with her and he also professed his love for her.
When she refused his advances, he threatened to commit suicide and stated that if she did not come to his house, he would die.

So, finding no way out on 14th August,
2023 at about 10.30 PM in the night, the victim accompanied the petitioner on his motor bike to his village.
They stayed in the house of the petitioner for two days.

Thereafter the petitioner and co-accused took her to Nayagarh and kept her in a rented house, where the petitioner kept physical relationship with her against her wishes and from there she was rescued by the police.

8. Mr. K. Rath, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is in custody since 20.08.2023 and the victim was aged more than 17 years at the time of occurrence and in the mean while the victim has been examined in the trial and the perusal of her deposition would reveal that she has gone voluntarily with the petitioner and also transferred money to his account on phonepe and there is no allegation of any use of force by the petitioner.

He further submits that since the victim had already been examined in the trial, no useful Page4 of 6 purpose will be served by detaining the petitioner in custody especially when 17 witnesses are still to be examined.

9. Mr. P. Tripathy, learned Additional Standing Counsel opposes the prayer for bail stating that the petitioner has betrayed the trust of the victim by having physical relationship with her in spite of her protest, which she has stated during her cross-examination.
He further submits that as 17 more witnesses are yet to be examined, the petitioner may try to influence prosecution witnesses, if he is released on bail.

10. Considering the age of the victim, the nature of allegations against the petitioner and as the victim has already been examined in the trial, I am inclined to allow his prayer for bail.
11.

The petitioner- Happy @ Manoj @ Jyotirmaya Swain shall be released on bail on such terms and conditions as may be fixed by the learned Court below in seisin over the matter, including the following conditions:
Happy @ Manoj @ Jyotirmaya vs State Of Orissa .....

(i) He will not commit any offence.
(ii) He will not tamper with prosecution evidence or try to influence prosecution witnesses while on bail.
Page5 of 6 (iii) He will appear on each date in the trial Court, once trial starts.
12. Violation of any condition will entail in cancellation of bail.
13. The BLAPL is accordingly disposed of.
14. Urgent certified copy of this order be granted on proper application.
